classification: engineering experiment and structural bound; no advance assumed
hypothesis: Compose a factor base as the Frobenius closure of a small seed space. Preserve that union exactly, solve S3 in component coordinates, and expose linear consequences before F4. Scaled proper-subfield seed spaces keep every mixed product space small; power-span seeds need mixed-Frobenius product ranks checked, not only their square-span rank.
construction: V_j=Frob_q^j(V), F={P:x(P) in union_j V_j}. Include every unordered component pair. Normalize (i,j) to (0,j-i) while applying inverse Frob_q^i to the target; store only one tensor per relative offset. Rational point lifting and group verification remain mandatory.

boundaries.prime_product_span: For nonzero U,V in GF(2^n), n prime, dim(UV)>=min(n,dim(U)+dim(V)-1), by linear Kneser. A proper subfield stabilizer can lower this bound only at composite extension degree.
boundaries.subfield_product: For K=GF(2^d) and V_i=alpha_i*K, span_F2(V_i*V_j)=alpha_i*alpha_j*K has dimension d for all i,j. This does not prove useful elliptic-curve relation yield.
boundaries.coverage: For B signed factor-base points, at most B(B+1)/2 distinct unordered pair sums are available. Uniform nonzero subgroup targets therefore have success probability <=min(1,B(B+1)/(2*(N-1))). Same-component-only pruning is an ablation and cannot claim completeness for the full union.
boundaries.chart_budget: With c distinct components, complete two-point coverage requires up to c(c+1)/2 component queries. All construction, rejected component pairs, failed targets, lifting and relation-matrix costs are charged.
boundaries.rho: Matched full-DLP rho is a reference where supported; total calibrated operation conversions remain unmeasured. No baseline or rho speedup is inferred from a smaller product span alone.

scope: Native binary S3 two-summand decomposition. The external frozen WDSat S4 executable does not call this encoding. Higher-arity chart composition and prime-field lifting are not implemented in this round.

structural.large_limit: 131-bit measurements are field-linear-algebra diagnostics only, never a DLP solve or runtime extrapolation. Verify field irreducibility first.

stage.split: 17 development, 937 fresh; same group targets for every factor-base family at fixed curve. Random seed spaces likewise use independent seeds.
stage.target_recipe: Seeded distinct nonzero prime-subgroup scalars, no planted decomposition bias. Complete unordered factor-base point-pair truth collected separately and withheld from solvers. Compare complete polynomial pair sets for charts, and first group witness for every oracle.
stage.same_component_ablation: Record how much exact coverage is lost if only same-component summands are allowed; do not use this incomplete ablation as the candidate.

frozen_regression.comparison: Rerun reference and candidate native S3 harness on every frozen and fresh target; existing default solver path remains off for chart experiments. Retain hashes and complete solution-set matches.

dlp.selection: Run all stage cases, including zero-column and low-yield controls; do not select winners by timing. Preserve incomplete and timed-out attempts.
dlp.verification: Disable direct-relation shortcuts; every claimed solve must recover the planted scalar and verify [k]P=Q. Same curve, base, target, seed, batch size and resources within each pair.

acceptance: Every completed root set and group witness must match independent truth. Treat as promising engineering only if fresh-target cold cost per verified relation improves >=20% over ambient F4 without lost coverage. Beating the strongest enumeration/pair-table baseline is a separate gate. An end-to-end advance requires calibrated total-cost, matched rho/floor ratios and preserved verified workload; otherwise leave those metrics null.
abandon: Reject any root loss, false refutation, uncharged chart branch, dropped timeout, silent fallback, mismatched field/curve/domain, or a subfield factor base whose projected columns vanish. A small product rank without net relation-cost benefit is a structural diagnostic, not a result.
